mutations.name: an empty query reaches the upstream — a blank search spends an upstream call and an upstream rate-limit slot on a request that cannot return anything
mutations.anchor: if (!q) return { ok: false, error: 'query required' };
mutations.replacement: if (false) return { ok: false, error: 'query required' };

mutations.name: the non-active guard is dropped — a disabled or errored account's likely-dead token is used anyway, turning a clear 'account is error' into an opaque upstream failure
mutations.anchor: if (account.status !== 'active') return { ok: false, error: `Account is ${account.status}` };
mutations.replacement: if (false) return { ok: false, error: `Account is ${account.status}` };

mutations.name: the untrimmed query is sent — leading/trailing whitespace changes the upstream cache/rate-limit key, so the same search counts as a different one
mutations.anchor: const results = await getWebSearchResults(account.apiKey, { query: q, limit, domain }, proxy);
mutations.replacement: const results = await getWebSearchResults(account.apiKey, { query, limit, domain }, proxy);

mutations.name: an upstream throw propagates instead of returning in-band — the dashboard gets a 500 on a dead token rather than a message it can render, breaking the convention every other account helper follows
mutations.anchor:
log.warn(`Web search failed for ${safeAccountRef(account)}: ${e.message}`);
    return { ok: false, error: e.message };

mutations.name: the unknown-account guard is dropped — a bogus id dereferences undefined and crashes the request instead of answering 'Account not found'
mutations.anchor:
if (!account) return { ok: false, error: 'Account not found' };
  // An error'd/disabled account's token is the likeliest to be dead; refusing here
